newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. says Zaire force still needed.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says Zaire force still needed.

text.p: The United Nations said on Friday it was delighted that up to 400,000 Rwandan refugees were heading home from eastern Zaire but a multinational force was still badly needed to help provide aid and logistics.
"Everybody is absolutely elated, but we still desperately need the multinational force," U.N. spokesman Sylvana Foa told Reuters.
She said the Geneva-based U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees was calling the huge exodus the "largest and fastest homeward movement of refugees in history."

"We have stocks in Rwanda for about 450,000 people, but we are going to need a lot of help to move these people around," she said, adding that only a military operation could provide the required logistics.

The Security Council was conferring privately on a draft resolution authorizing a multinational force, to be led by Canada, to help deliver humanitarian aid for the refugees and their voluntary, orderly repatriation.

It was not immediately clear what effect news of the spontaneous return of hundreds of thousands of refugees might have on the council's deliberations and whether the force might eventually need fewer than the 10,000 troops currently proposed.
